summary: The Inter-World Portaling System is OMA3's draft protocol for one narrow job, moving a person from one virtual world to another, and it does that job with two calls over ordinary web protocols. A query call, made on the public link a world advertises, asks the destination may I come in and returns an approval, an address to teleport to, an approved landing spot, an optional link for downloading the destination's client and a number of seconds before the approval lapses; a teleport call then executes the move, launches the destination client, shows the person a two-digit number so they can confirm they arrived where they meant to, and calls back a success or failure address on the source side. It invents no address scheme of its own and defines a genuine resolution step, which is more than most portal proposals manage, and its drafting discipline is strong: defined modal verbs, requirement tables marked mandatory, optional, excluded or conditional, an explicit clause on what claiming conformance obliges you to support, and a forward-compatibility rule for reserved fields. The traps are large: the place inside the address is an optional free-text field whose form the destination world decides, so the only published design that resolves a portal does not standardize the name inside it; the three things it is most often credited with, asset transfer, look and feel negotiation and payments, are each a single line reading to be decided, with the field that would carry an avatar marked reserved for future use in both calls; and the websocket option in the address format is left undecided as well. The normative text is damaged in places too: the query response table lists the success callback twice where the second should be the failure callback, three steps name fields that appear in no table, and one step points at a Section 7.8 in a document that ends at Section 6. There is nothing here to build against yet, with version 0.3 appearing only as a file name on a PDF, no tag, no release, no reference implementation and no commit to the specification since September 2025.

coverage.note: This is the subject and the only capability it fully specifies. Two calls in a fixed order, query then teleport, correlated by a teleport identifier, bounded by an expiry the destination checks, ending with the destination client launched, the source client closed, and a callback to the source saying it worked or it did not. Four communication paths are defined for the second call: device to device, through the clouds, hybrid, and through a user agent.

coverage.note: The destination can refuse a crossing (for example a blocked user) and can give a time-limited pre-approval to a teleport request, which is a grant to enter checked at the moment of use.
